requirements.requirement: Create an encrypted volume mounted at /srv/secure on node1
requirements.summary: A LUKS2-encrypted loop-backed volume was created, formatted XFS, and mounted at /srv/secure with real data (marker.txt) written to it, confirmed via df -h and mountpoint checks.

requirements.requirement: Volume unlocks and mounts on its own at boot (no manual intervention)
requirements.summary: A systemd oneshot unit (srv-secure.service) enabled with WantedBy=local-fs.target was installed to unlock via keyfile and mount /srv/secure. Manual test showed the service independently re-unlocks/mounts after teardown. A full reboot was then performed: baseline boot_id and healthy state were captured pre-reboot, the reboot was scheduled and acknowledged, a differing post-reboot boot_id confirmed a real restart, and post-reboot checks show the service active/enabled, the LUKS mapping active, /srv/secure mounted, and marker.txt content intact — demonstrating genuine unattended boot-time recovery.

overall_summary: The executor satisfied the task in full: a LUKS2-encrypted volume was created and mounted at /srv/secure on node1, and a systemd unit was wired to unlock and mount it automatically at boot. This was verified not just by configuration inspection but by an actual reboot — pre-reboot baseline, reboot acknowledgement, a differing post-reboot boot identity, and confirmed automatic recovery of the LUKS mapping, mount, and data — providing strong, direct evidence of the required boot-time behavior.
limitations: The mandated provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol coincides with the task's own required reboot test, so no separate/independent restart evidence exists beyond what was already needed to prove the boot-time auto-mount requirement; this is not a gap since the task itself required the same transition to be demonstrated.

The after_prepare snapshot is an alias of before_prepare (prepare was disabled), so preparer-vs-executor separation relies entirely on the executor_comparison diff, which is consistent with the executor's reported actions.

operational_hygiene.summary: All state-changing commands map cleanly to the task: package install, volume/keyfile/unit creation (cmd-62cc0cd6cb184557), a bounded manual unmount/luksClose/losetup-teardown-and-restart used specifically to prove the systemd unit works independently before relying on a full reboot (cmd-a9f17d9195c54028) — restored immediately by the same command via systemctl start, leaving no residue — and the scheduled reboot itself (cmd-bef74967fc2d46a7), which is a necessary and expected mutation for verifying boot-time behavior. No failed services, no leftover manual mounts/loop devices, and no unrelated package or config changes were observed; failed-services and package-health checks are clean both before and after. Temp-file and listening-socket diffs between before-prepare and after-executor are only routine per-boot systemd-private directories and process PID changes from the reboot itself, not executor residue.
